title: Add tests for customer tier mapping edge cases (dedicated/private flags, pilot credits)
author: Caleb Johnson
description: Context: We’ve had a few near-misses (and one minor backfill discrepancy) where `customer_tier` was derived differently depending on which upstream flags were present (dedicated routing metadata vs contract flags) and where some pilot/credit-only customers were incorrectly classified as enterprise. This PR adds targeted test coverage around tier derivation to prevent regressions as we continue to iterate on mapping rules for the Unit Economics dashboard. Changes: (1) Adds a comprehensive unit test matrix for tier derivation covering precedence rules between `dedicated`, `private`, `enterprise_contract`, `reseller`, and `pilot_credits`/`free_credits` flags. (2) Adds “golden” fixtures for known edge cases pulled from real anonymized records (IDs removed; synthetic account keys used). (3) Adds a few property-style tests to assert invariants (e.g., dedicated/private always win over self-serve; pilot credits never implicitly upgrade tier; unknown inputs map to `self_serve` + `tier_confidence=low`). (4) Extends backfill tooling tests to ensure historical rows don’t silently shift tiers when optional fields are missing. Notes/decisions encoded in tests: - Precedence: private > dedicated > enterprise > self_serve. - Reseller is treated as enterprise for v1 reporting but is emitted as `enterprise` with `tier_source=reseller_contract` (we don’t expose reseller as a separate tier yet). - `pilot_credits=true` does not upgrade a customer out of self-serve unless `enterprise_contract=true` (aligns with Finance methodology). - If both dedicated and private flags are set (shouldn’t happen, but has in older logs), we map to private and emit a warning metric (asserted in tests). Testing: `bazel test //analytics/...` and `//telemetry/...` plus added coverage run; see CI. Rollout: No prod behavior change expected (tests only), but this is a gate for future edits to tier mapping logic. Related: ENG-8423 (tier derivation) and ENG-8429 (data quality checks).
commits: test(analytics): add tier mapping fixture builder helpers
test(unit-econ): cover pilot credits + free credits edge cases
test(backfill): ensure missing optional fields don’t shift tiers
chore(ci): wire tier mapping tests into analytics test target
review_conversation: Logan Wright (review): Can we make the precedence explicit in one place rather than spread across multiple tests? Also please confirm how we want to treat reseller right now (separate tier vs enterprise). Caleb Johnson (author): Good call. I added a `TierCase` table-driven matrix test with an inline precedence comment and kept the other tests for invariants only. For reseller: aligning with Finance/PRD, we map reseller -> enterprise for v1; I added `tier_source=reseller_contract` in the expected output so we can split later without re-mapping history. Nadia Rahman (review): The pilot credits case is the one that bit us last month—can we add a regression test that reproduces the exact failure mode (missing `enterprise_contract` + present `pilot_credits`)? Caleb Johnson (author): Added fixture `pilot_credits_missing_contract_maps_self_serve` with the minimal set of fields that previously triggered the incorrect enterprise classification. Mei Lin (review): Backfill stability test is great. One nit: can we avoid asserting exact warning log strings? They tend to change. Caleb Johnson (author): Updated to assert the warning metric increment (`tier_conflict_private_and_dedicated_total`) instead of the log message. Cole Summers (approve): LGTM. These tests should help keep the economics numbers stable while we keep iterating on contract tagging.
release_notes: Internal: Adds regression coverage for customer tier mapping edge cases used by Unit Economics aggregation (no behavior change).
